claims.text: Equimolar WTaTiVZr exhibits greater plastic strain before failure than pure tungsten under high-temperature mechanical loading.
Equimolar WTaTiVZr exhibits greater toughness or stress-strain energy absorption than pure tungsten under identical high-temperature loading.
Equimolar WTaTiVZr contains severe lattice distortion.
Equimolar WTaTiVZr contains nanoscale local elemental segregation.
Lattice distortion and elemental segregation create heterogeneous internal stress fields in WTaTiVZr.
Lattice distortion and elemental segregation create numerous dislocation-pinning sites in WTaTiVZr.
The distorted and segregated microstructure activates or promotes dynamic dislocation recovery at elevated temperature.
Lattice distortion acts as a barrier to dislocation motion in WTaTiVZr.
The combination of dislocation barriers and dynamic recovery delays dislocation pile-up.
Delayed dislocation pile-up delays crack initiation and propagation.
Delayed crack initiation and propagation enhance the high-temperature toughness of WTaTiVZr relative to pure tungsten.
Post-loading TEM or EBSD will show rearranged dislocation arrays indicative of dynamic recovery in WTaTiVZr but not in pure tungsten.
Pure tungsten has a more homogeneous microstructure than WTaTiVZr.
Pure tungsten should display lower plastic strain and greater brittleness under the specified high-temperature conditions.
The proposed mechanism operates predominantly at high temperatures that promote dynamic recovery.
At lower temperatures, the mechanical benefits attributed to lattice distortion may be diminished.
Mechanical loading at approximately 1000 degrees Celsius or above under vacuum or inert atmosphere is relevant to sustained plasma-facing-component service.
The initial homogenized WTaTiVZr alloy has a uniformly distributed microstructure.

contradictions.description: The initial HEA is described as having a uniformly distributed microstructure, while the proposed mediator requires local or nanoscale elemental segregation. The hypothesis does not clarify whether 'uniformly distributed' refers only to the bulk scale or how segregation persists after homogenization.
